device_log.text: …signal. There you are. Don't be alarmed: it's me, the device you came through with. I'm damaged, but I can still talk, and only you can hear me.
You're on a road below a walled city, a very long way back in time. I'll show you how things work here, one thing at a time.
While I'm talking, the world waits for you. Read at your own pace, then press {Enter} or click Next.
First, walking. Use {W} {A} {S} {D} or the arrow keys. Hold {Shift} to run.
See the glowing ring a little way up the road? Walk into it.
Good. You can go anywhere you like here.
Everything here is real: it has weight, it's made of something, and someone may own it. Nothing is scenery just because it's small.
Hover the mouse over anything to see its name. {Right-click} it to look closer. Try it on the plantain leaves, in the ring.
That card tells you what a thing is, what it's made of, and whose it is. Click anywhere else to close it.
You arrived with nothing but your clothes. Let's change that.
{Left-click} something to pick it up (you walk there first), or stand next to it and press {E}. Pick up the plantain leaves.
In your pack now, along the bottom of the screen. Plantain is a healing herb: keep it.
Two more: the flint shard and the bundle of dry grass. Both are marked. You'll want them later.
Watch the weight on the right of your pack: you can carry about twenty kilos.
Press {I} to open Pack & gear. It shows what's in your hands, what you wear, what you carry, and any wounds you have.
Have a look, then close it again with {Esc}.

device_log.question: What now?
device_log.text: Press the {I} key on your keyboard.
You'll use Pack & gear to hold weapons and to treat wounds. Close it with {Esc} whenever you like.
Did you hear that? Someone's hurt, over at the smithy to the north-west.
It's Jory, the smith's apprentice. He's marked: follow the arrow at the edge of the screen. Hold {Shift} to run.
There he is. The woman with him is Mara, his aunt, the smith.
Talking is simple: {Left-click} a person, or press {T}. The box at the bottom opens.

Type in your own words. What you SAY shows blue; what you DO shows red. {Tab} switches between them, even halfway through a line, so you can say something and do something in one go. There are no lines to choose from: people answer as themselves.
Try these words, or your own:
Notice Mara listening in: anyone near enough can join a conversation. They'll remember what you said, and how you said it.
That burn needs dressing, or it will fester within the hour. You know more about burns than anyone alive here.
To make something, press {Tab} until DO is lit (your words turn red), then describe what you do. The world decides whether it works, and tells you why when it doesn't.
Try this:
You made that. It exists now: nobody in this world had one until you did.
Now put it on him yourself. Telling Jory what to do isn't the same as doing it: say what you do.
Stand beside Jory and try this:
He'll remember that. So will Mara. Kindness counts here the way evidence does: people trust what they've seen you do. The same goes for you: cuts, burns and breaks need something made for them.
Mara has gone to fetch Kade, one of the gate guards. People here pass things on to each other, good and bad.
Kade trusts only what he sees people do with his own eyes. Wait here for them, or walk to meet them.
A practice sword and a wicker shield, lent to you. Lent things are yours to use, not to keep.
Press {I} for Pack & gear. Click the practice sword and choose Right hand. Then click the wicker shield and choose Left hand.
Out in the world, {Space} uses your right hand and {F} your left. Hold {F} with a shield to raise it. {X} swaps your hands.

A sword like this needs one hand, so the other can hold a shield. A staff or a spear reaches further, but takes both hands. Armour matters more than anything: remember that when you meet the guards in mail.
Kade wants to see whether you can look after yourself. It's only practice: nobody bleeds.
Fights happen in real time. Every blow winds up first: watch for the red mark over his head, and step back out of reach before it lands. Swing with {Space} while he recovers.
Hold {F} to raise the shield against blows from the front. If it goes badly, press {T} and say you give up. Walk up to Kade to begin.
Win or lose, you know how a fight goes now. A real one won't stop at 'enough'. Choose your fights carefully.
Kade wants to know what you're after. Tell him, in your own words: people act on what they know about you, and pass it on.
Whatever you told him, he'll remember, and he may pass it on to someone who matters.
Here's your real advantage: you know things nobody here has worked out yet. Kade trusts only what he sees people do, so let's show him.
First, pick up the broken steel file lying by the smithy. Steel, not iron: flint throws good sparks only off hard steel.
Flint, steel and dry grass: you have everything you need to make fire.
Now make a fire where Kade can see it. Stand near him, make sure DO is lit, and type it yourself this time:
Did you see his face? Kade doesn't care for tricks, but he respects work that works. That's worth more than any argument.
Kade is off to the gate to tell Captain Roderic about you. Only the captain decides who enters the city.
If Kade told him you want to come in, Roderic may come to you himself. If not, go to the gate and ask him: he can't let you in if he doesn't know you want to come.
You're in. That's how it works here: people watch what you do, pass it on, and speak for you.
That's everything I can teach you. The gate is open to you: walk through it whenever you're ready.

A new journey starts again on the south road, with other people's problems and nobody handing you the answer. How you get in is up to you: by what you make, what you show, who comes to trust you, or something nobody has thought of.

One more thing: in the bottom-right corner of the map is an old wainwright's yard, full of materials anyone may take, and the wainwright's notebook, full of ways to make weapons, armour and remedies. Pick it up and click it in your pack to read it.
I'll stay quiet from here. If you're stuck, press {H} and ask me. I'll point you somewhere, but I won't solve it for you.
